subject: Business Models
title: Chick-fil-A's Unusual Model
description: A fast breakdown of Chick-fil-A's Unusual Model for builders.

hook.text: Chick-fil-A's franchise fee is just $10,000. McDonald's costs $1 million+. There's a catch.

buildup.text: Chick-fil-A owns everything: the building, the equipment, the kitchen. The operator just runs it.

discovery.text: Chick-fil-A takes 15% of sales plus 50% of profits. Operators keep less but invest almost nothing upfront.

twist.text: Chick-fil-A accepts only 0.4% of applicants. It's harder to become a franchise operator than to get into Harvard.

climax.text: This selectivity drives quality. Chick-fil-A's per-store revenue is double McDonald's despite being closed Sundays.

punchline.text: $10,000 to start, 0.4% acceptance rate. Selectivity creates excellence.

quiz.question: What percentage of Chick-fil-A franchise applicants are accepted?

details.summary: Chick-fil-A requires only a 10,000-dollar initial investment from operators but retains ownership of the restaurant and equipment. Operators earn a salary plus a percentage of profits..
details.whyItMatters: Chick-fil-A generates over 8 million dollars in average unit revenue, more than double McDonald's. Its model proves that extreme operator selection and low financial barriers can produce better results than the traditional high-investment franchise.
takeaways: Operators invest only 10,000 dollars while Chick-fil-A owns the building and equipment
Average unit revenue exceeds 8 million dollars, more than double McDonald's per-store average
The company accepts less than 1 percent of franchise applicants for operator positions

faq.question: How does Chick-fil-A's franchise model differ from traditional franchises?
faq.answer: Chick-fil-A owns the restaurant, real estate, and equipment. Operators invest only 10,000 dollars versus hundreds of thousands at other chains. Operators cannot own multiple units or pass the business to heirs. The company retains far more control but removes financial barriers to entry.

faq.question: Why does Chick-fil-A's model produce such high unit volumes?
faq.answer: Extreme operator selection from over 60,000 annual applicants ensures exceptional leadership. Single-unit focus prevents distracted multi-unit management. Closed Sundays create scarcity and rest. Corporate ownership alignment means the company invests in each location's success.
